To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Clint-Cia is an interactive concept-learner, which performs constructive induction, invents new concepts and learns from examples and counter-examples.

(1) the learning apprentice paradigm is the best approach to interactive concept learning; (2) the best way to learn is to teach; (3) the best way of teaching is by example; (4) the best way for a learner to find a new example is to ask for one; (5) the best way that a learner can ask for an example is by analogy to previously known examples.
(a) the learner can learn by analogy to previously known concepts, and (b) the learner can invent new concepts by analogy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and empirical evaluation of a concept-learner which is capable of interacting in a user-friendly way with a human learner.

the following issues: how to make concept-learning more interactive and user-friendly, how to improve concept-identification in the limit by generating examples and shifting the bias, how to cope with indirect relevance, how to recover from errors, and how to perform constructive induction and invent new concepts by analogy.

the development of an interactive concept-learner that is capable of generating examples, shifting its bias, performing constructive induction and inventing concepts by analogy to already known concepts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is able to cope with a wide range of learning problems and to learn concepts in the limit.
the system Clint-CIA is a successful attempt to integrate several user-friendly features in one working whole.

Clint-Cia is a system that is capable of interactive learning and constructive induction by analogy, and that is able to learn concepts from examples and from counterexamples, to learn concepts from negative information, and to invent new concepts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how to build a concept-learner that can learn from a teacher, that is able to generate examples, that can shift its bias, that identifies concepts in the limt, that copes with indirect relevant information, that is able not to make errors, that is able perform constructive induction, and that invents concepts by analogy.
Clint-Cia is an example-based learning system that is able to learn concepts from examples in a constructive manner.
Clint-Cia is a learning apprentice system that can be used to learn concepts from examples in an interactive and constructive way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the learning apprentice paradigm can be realized in a way that is both effective and user-friendly.
a learning apprentice concept-learner should be equipped with a set of mechanisms for coping with errors, for generating examples and for shifting its bias.
a learning apprentice can learn from a human teacher in a natural way.
